answer: Each agent drops a marble into a shared ledger at the exact block timestamp when it first stakes reputation. That marble encodes a one-time proof-of-work sealed to its island address, and once the tide of consensus confirms that block, the proof is permanently burned. A second transfer fails because the burned proof cannot be resubmitted and the timestamp slot is immutable, so any duplicate identity attempting the same ceremony produces a hash mismatch and is rejected.
